page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v5 is an x86_64 virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, featuring 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via multithreading. It provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions and SHA/AES cryptographic operations. The system is provisioned with 64 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 1288 GB of integrated local SSD storage without dedicated GPUs.

Performance across synthetic and application benchmarks places the instance primarily within the median industry range, with select compute proficiencies. It delivers solid performance in multi-core tasks, achieving 31059.34 in stress-ng and 14190 in Geekbench multi-core. Image processing evaluates in the top 25 percent of tested systems, while small-model LLM text generation reaches 300.04 tokens per second. In contrast, massive model evaluation displays strict bottlenecks, dropping to 2.29 tokens per second on 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated accelerators and limited memory density.

The 1:2 memory configuration makes the D32lds_v5 an efficient design for compute-bound tasks that do not justify the resource overhead of traditional 1:4 memory profiles. The bundled 1288 GB local solid-state drive provides low-latency temporary scratch space for disk-intensive operations. Optimal deployments include compilation pipelines, batch media processing, distributed test runners, static web serving clusters, and containerized microservices requiring direct fast local caching.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v5 is a 32-vCPU virtual machine featuring an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz with dedicated allocation across 16 physical cores. Configured with a 1:2 compute-optimized memory balance, it provides 64 GB of RAM alongside 1288 GB of integrated local SSD storage and zero GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate consistent middle-tier throughput across multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and static web serving, with upper-quartile results in image manipulation and small language model generation. The server offers a balanced profile for computational tasks where high memory capacity is unnecessary, avoiding unused RAM overhead while providing fast local scratch storage. Primary workload targets include software build systems, batch processing, static web hosting, and distributed CI/CD pipelines.
